mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 2% triggers a risk premium adjustment that pushes S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.0 in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative when CPIAUCSL > 2%, or the t-statistic for the return difference is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index above the prior month's level coincides with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to increased wage growth depressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: In regimes where PAYEMS rises for 3 consecutive months, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in at least 80% of cases (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO supply index below 100 signals tight supply conditions that raise the cost of capital, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over a 5-year window, no significant positive return is observed when INDPRO < 100 for at least 4 consecutive months (Granger causality test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST retail sales above 100 triggers a short-term demand expansion that is associated with positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive months where HOUST > 100, the 5-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of instances (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to higher real borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25 pp in the current month
failure_condition: Over 10 such FEDFUNDS increases, the average 20-day forward return is non-negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 5% for two consecutive months reduces labor market tightness, resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE < 5% for at least 6 months, the 60-day forward return is non-negative in over 70% of cases (frequency).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 (demand) and RSAFS (demand) while FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.1% creates a dual pressure that produces negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prev and RSAFS < prev and FEDFUNDS > prev + 0.1 pp
failure_condition: In 100 such interaction events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in more than 50% (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis recovery regime (defined by UNRATE < 6% and INDPRO > 105), S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive due to normalization of risk premia.
failure_condition: In the regime window, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 30% of observations (frequency).
